description: Channels added to, removed from or reordered in a polyphonic signal, in 2HP, with a trigger that shifts or shuffles the order

params.text: Makes the channel knob follow the input while it is green, and lets you set the count by hand while it is dark
Sets how many channels come out, 1 to 16, and is ignored while the button above it is green
Chooses what fills a channel added beyond the input: Vl uses the value knob, Rp repeats the input channels round again
Sets the voltage of channels added beyond the input, -10V to +10V, and fills every channel when nothing is patched
Puts the channel order back to the order of the input
Chooses what a trigger does to the order: Nxt shifts the channels up, Prv shifts them down, Shfl rearranges them at random
Shifts or shuffles the channel order by hand, exactly as a trigger does

inputs.text: The polyphonic signal whose channels are counted and reordered
A rising edge puts the channel order back to the order of the input
A rising edge shifts or shuffles the channel order, according to the order switch

outputs.text: Carries the input's channels at the count and in the order set here

notes: the sixteen lights across the top are the output channels; the colour runs green to red to show which input channel each one is carrying, and hovering one names that channel
a light at half brightness marks a channel added beyond what the input has
with the count set above the input and the order shuffled, a downstream module reading only channel 1 gets a probability switch, the odds being the input count over the output count
menu: Light brightness-scale: 5V (e.g. bipolar -5V to +5V), 10V (e.g. unipolar 0V to +10V) — sets the voltage the channel lights are scaled against
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
Trigger-high detect-level — sets the voltage at which an incoming trigger counts as high, 1V or more unless you change it
Trigger-low detect-level — sets the voltage an incoming trigger must fall back below before the next one is counted, under 0.1V unless you change it

inputs.1:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
